@graph.headline: Building a Research Intelligence System: How I Use AI Agents for Daily Knowledge Operations
@graph.description: An architectural breakdown of the multi-agent research system powering FrankX.AI: five specialized agents, three workflow modes, and a publication pipeline optimized for the AI age.
@graph.keywords: ai research system, multi-agent workflow, claude code research, knowledge management ai, research automation, generative engine optimization
@graph.abstract: The FrankX Research Intelligence System deploys five coordinated agents across three operational modes: Signal Intake, Deep Research, and Publication. This multi-agent pipeline compresses 40-hour manual investigation cycles into structured, citation-verified knowledge packages ready for distribution.

mainEntity.name: What are the three modes of the Research Intelligence System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mode 1 handles rapid signal intake, Mode 2 executes deep research investigations, and Mode 3 formats verified findings for publication.

mainEntity.name: How do research agents verify sources?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agents score source credibility on a multi-tier trust hierarchy, cross-referencing claims across primary documentation before inclusion.

mainEntity.name: What agents make up the research team?

acceptedAnswer.text: Signal Scout, Deep Researcher, Synthesis Engine, Fact Validator, and Editorial Architect.
Outputs are compiled as version-controlled markdown dossiers with structured frontmatter and verified reference citations.

mainEntity.name: How does this system support generative engine optimization?

acceptedAnswer.text: By structuring research findings with high Information Gain and clean data tables that search engines cite directly.
